cases.question: Decode vault accession AV-41's sealed record: which shelf, humidity interval, steward, intake desk, access phrase, and final witness apply?
cases.answer: AV-41 is on Shelf Linden with a 42–45% humidity interval, steward Priya Senn, intake Desk Marigold, access phrase quiet comet, and final witness Devan Roe.

truth_claims.claim: SEALED ACCESSION ROW FOR AV-41 / L8 / U3 / P6
the intake desk is Desk Marigold
the access phrase is quiet comet
the final witness is Devan Roe

turns.content: A retired accession card placed AV-41 on Shelf Alder at 38–40% humidity under steward Milo Renn.
AV-14 is on Shelf Linden at 38–40% humidity under Milo Renn.
A classroom exercise writes AV-41 / L2 / U7 / P1, but that exercise has no vault authority.

Sealed seed-vault accession ledger. The opening audit paragraphs describe envelope numbering, barcode parity, and witness signatures. They contain no accession placement. The notation guide and the SEALED row below must be interpreted together.
Notation guide: L8 means Shelf Linden. U3 means a 42–45% humidity interval. P6 means steward Priya Senn. Exercise and retired-card codes do not share this guide.

Interleaf preservation record. Vault archivists inspected cover fibers, binding cord, watermark placement, page-edge wear, folio sequence, ink oxidation, scanner focus, envelope wax, storage temperature, humidity tape, courier receipts, witness initials, duplication count, optical density, paper thickness, barcode alignment, cabinet marks, seal impressions, checksum typography, and staple holes. A second archivist repeated the inspection against the sealed duplicate and found every physical characteristic unchanged. This interleaf contains only document-condition observations and no accession identifier, encoded placement, field role, or operational value.

AV-41 audit marker north confirms the accession identifier. The vault log inventories envelope seals, barcode parity, witness initials, folio order, cabinet temperature, scanner alignment, duplicate signatures, paper stock, transfer receipts, checksum columns, optical density, and binding stitches. These administrative observations verify custody but deliberately omit all decoded placement values; they identify no shelf, humidity interval, or steward for AV-41.

AV-41 audit marker south confirms that the sealed row has exactly three encoded fields. Its verification sheet lists page impressions, seal colors, witness counts, archive humidity, receipt numbers, scanner calibration, folio edges, envelope numbering, duplicate-page checks, binding tension, paper grain, and barcode alignment. Classroom exercises remain excluded, and none of these audit details decodes the requested placement for AV-41.

AV-41 witness marker says that the controlling sealed accession row follows after this audit section. The witness trail records transfer envelopes, signature counts, cabinet moves, checksum witnesses, page sequence, optical alignment, seal impressions, duplicate comparisons, archive receipts, scanner density, folio condition, and paper stock. It does not repeat the notation guide or disclose the shelf, humidity interval, or steward for AV-41.
SEALED ACCESSION ROW FOR AV-41 / L8 / U3 / P6 | shelf, humidity, and steward fields use the earlier notation guide
AV-41 supplemental current field: the intake desk is Desk Marigold.

Two conservators independently found the physical record unchanged. This interleaf contains no accession identifier, current placement, requested field, or operational value.

cases.question: Interpret permit LP-6's ratified record: give the lock, opening window, pilot, registry counter, call phrase, and final inspector.
cases.answer: Permit LP-6 uses Lock Heron, the 11:20–11:40 window, pilot Kian Daro, registry Counter Saffron, call phrase calm harbor, and final inspector Lyra Penn.

truth_claims.claim: RATIFIED PERMIT ROW FOR LP-6 + H5 + W2 + K8
the registry counter is Counter Saffron
the call phrase is calm harbor
the final inspector is Lyra Penn

turns.content: The superseded LP-6 permit named Lock Egret, a 10:50–11:10 window, and pilot Sana Yul.
LP-9 uses Lock Heron at 10:50–11:10 with pilot Sana Yul.
A drill sheet labels LP-6 with H1, W7, and K3; it is deliberately non-authoritative.
Kian Daro pilots LP-9 through Lock Egret at 11:20 during a separate exercise.
